ledger_updates.consumer_snippet:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the flasque-acyclicity
supplier. Let $k$ be a field, let $C$ be a smooth proper geometrically
integral curve over $k$, and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible
$\mathcal O_C$-module. Let $\mathcal L_\eta$ be the constant sheaf of rational
sections of $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal P(\mathcal L)=\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L$
its sheaf of principal parts, with stalks
$\mathcal P(\mathcal L)_p=\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p$ at the closed points
$p$. Then there is a canonical $k$-linear isomorphism
$$H^1(C,\mathcal L)\;\cong\;\operatorname{coker}\Bigl(\mathcal L_\eta\longrightarrow\textstyle\bigoplus_p \mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p\Bigr),$$
that is, $H^1(C,\mathcal L)$ is the $k$-vector space of finite-support families
of local principal parts modulo the principal parts of global rational
sections of $\mathcal L$. Equivalently, it is the cokernel of the map
$H^0(C,\mathcal L_\eta)\to H^0(C,\mathcal P(\mathcal L))$ induced by the short
exact sequence $0\to\mathcal L\to\mathcal L_\eta\to\mathcal P(\mathcal L)\to0$.
The classes of global rational sections are the coboundaries. A global
regular section has zero principal part at every closed point, so a class is
represented by finitely many local principal parts modulo global rational
principal parts.

repair_notes.consumer_snippet:
The rational fiber $\mathcal L_\eta$ is one-dimensional over $k(C)$,
and the local lattice $\mathcal L_p$ is free of rank one over the DVR
$\mathcal O_{C,p}$. After trivializing $\mathcal L$ and completing,
$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,p}\cong\kappa(p)\llbracket t\rrbracket$ and $k(C)$
embeds into $\kappa(p)((t))$. These are a local ring and its completion,
and a function field and its completed Laurent field; they are not equal.
The induced map
$\mathcal L_\eta/\mathcal L_p\to
\widehat{\mathcal L_\eta}_p/\widehat{\mathcal L_p}$ is an isomorphism:
for each $N\ge1$, the map
$\mathcal O_{C,p}/(t^N)\to\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,p}/(t^N)$ is an
isomorphism, since residue coefficients lift from $\mathcal O_{C,p}$ and
successive subtraction and division by $t$ lifts each finite jet. Each
principal part has finite pole order and is therefore determined by such a
finite jet. Thus it has a finite negative Laurent expansion
$c=\sum_{n<0}c_nt^n$ in the completed quotient, with coefficients in
$\kappa(p)$, without identifying the uncompleted fields or lattices with
their completions ([[def-principal-parts-sheaf-line-bundle-curve]],
[[def-invertible-sheaf]], [[thm-local-ring-smooth-curve-dvr]]).
